title: Data Sciences, B.S. (Eberly College of Science)
notes: Statistical Modeling option, University Park (plan code DTSCS_BS), built from the real 2023-24 archived bulletin edition (bulletins.psu.edu/archive/2023-2024/undergraduate/colleges/eberly-science/data-sciences-bs/, raw HTML fetched directly; Suggested Academic Plan prints Total Credits 126 for the University Park table, and its own Fall/Spring subtotals -- 15/16, 17/15, 15/15, 16.5/16.5 -- sum to that 126 correctly). REAL DIFFERENCES FOUND vs. the 2026 file, and vs. the 2022-23 edition (DS-2022.json): (1) STAT 184 is still genuinely a 2-credit course in this edition (confirmed directly against the archived STAT course-description page for this same 2023-24 edition: 'STAT 184: Introduction to R -- 2 Credits'), and this edition's own UP Suggested Academic Plan table itself also correctly prints 2 (unlike the 2022-23 edition's own table, which had an isolated 1-credit typo in that one cell). STAT 184 doesn't become a real 3-credit course until the 2024-25 edition (see that file's notes) -- modeled here as 'credits': 2, informational label only, same shared-catalog caveat as DS-2022.json. (2) The extra all-options 'STAT/MATH 318 or 418' Common Requirement present in the 2022-23 edition is GONE from this edition's Common Requirements section -- it moved to being specific to the Applied Data Sciences option only (which doesn't otherwise take a probability course), confirmed directly from this edition's own Program Requirements text. Statistical Modeling students in this edition do NOT take STAT/MATH 318/418 -- no such item is included in this file, matching this edition's real requirements (contrast with DS-2022.json, which does include it for that earlier edition only). (3) IST 210 (present in the 2022-23 edition's own Suggested Plan table, see that file's notes) is confirmed GONE from this edition's own Suggested Academic Plan table -- not included here either, consistent both ways. (4) CMPSC 465 (or DS 305) is still NOT a required course in this edition -- same as 2022-23, this edition's own Suggested Academic Plan table has no such required line (it only shows up starting with the 2024-25 edition, see that file's notes); CMPSC 465 here remains only one of several interchangeable List B elective options. (5) List A / List B Statistical Modeling option course enumeration is directly confirmed on this edition's own page, identical to the 2022-23 edition: List A (6 credits required) = MATH 435, (MATH 436 or MATH 441), (MATH 451 or MATH 455), MATH 484, (MATH 416/STAT 416), STAT 461, STAT 463, STAT 466, STAT 483; List B (6 credits required) = DS 320, DS 330, DS 410, DS 402, IST 461, CMPSC 442, CMPSC 465. Modeled the same way as DS-2022.json: two 3-credit slots per list (6+6=12 total), matching this edition's own stated DTSCS_BS option total of 38 credits. (6) MATH 220 prints at 2 credits in this edition's own Suggested Plan table too (matching math_catalog.json's fixed 2.0), same as 2022-23 -- no discrepancy to flag (contrast with 2024-25/2025-26, see those files' notes). (7) MATH 21 has no prerequisite of its own in the current shared math_catalog.json -- same finding and same resolution as DS-2022.json (MATH 21 alone, no MATH 3/4 filler chain needed); confirmed via build_full_plan (0 'Could not schedule' warnings). Structurally, the 2023-24 edition's Statistical Modeling option Prescribed/Additional/Supporting course lists (MATH 230, STAT/MATH 414, STAT/MATH 415, STAT 440, STAT 462, DS 200/STAT 200, DS 310/CMPSC 448, MATH 311W/CMPSC 360, List A, List B) are byte-for-byte identical to the 2022-23 edition's own option text -- confirmed by direct comparison of both editions' raw fetched pages. GRADUATION TIMELINE: same finding as DS-2022.json -- this file's item set (no MATH 3/MATH 4 filler, and this edition also has neither the extra STAT 318 course nor the CMPSC 465/DS 305 requirement) fits cleanly in the standard 4 years/8 terms: confirmed via build_full_plan with a same-era start_year=2023/today=2023-07-01 control run at grad_years=4 -- 0 warnings, goal met. Does not itself need the grad_years=5 override Backend/tests.py already carries for DS (that override exists for the 2026 edition's own extra padding, see DS-2022.json's notes finding (7); it applies uniformly across DS's catalog years and this file still passes cleanly under it too).
